title: Efficacy and Safety of Intravenous Efzofitimod in Patients With Pulmonary Sarcoidosis
off: A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Intravenous Efzofitimod in Patients With Pulmonary Sarcoidosis
summary: This is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, study comparing the efficacy and safety of intravenous (IV) efzofitimod 3 mg/kg and 5 mg/kg versus placebo after 48 weeks of treatment. This study will enroll adults with histologically confirmed pulmonary sarcoidosis receiving stable treatment with oral corticosteroid (OCS), with or without immunosuppressant therapy.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Documented history of pulmonary sarcoidosis for at least 6 months, supported by the following evidence: documented histologically proven diagnosis of sarcoidosis by tissue biopsy and documented evidence of parenchymal lung involvement by historical radiological evidence
* Evidence of symptomatic pulmonary sarcoidosis, as demonstrated by the following criteria: Modified Medical Research Council (MRC) dyspnea scale grade of at least 1 and KSQ-Lung score ≤70
* Patients must be receiving treatment with OCS of ≥ 3 months at Day 1 with a starting dose between ≥ 7.5 and ≤ 25 mg/day ≥ 4 weeks prior to Day 1.
* Body weight ≥ 40 kg and \< 160 kg

Exclusion Criteria:

* Treatment with \> 1 immunosuppressant therapy
* Treatment with biological immunomodulators, such as tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) inhibitors or antifibrotics or interleukin inhibitors
* Likelihood of significant pulmonary fibrosis as shown by any 1 or more of the following: High resolution CT fibrosis \> 20% within the last 12 months; FVC percent predicted (FVCPP) \< 50% and KSQ-Lung score \< 30
* In the opinion of the investigator, clinically significant pulmonary hypertension
* Patients with active cardiac, neuro, or renal sarcoidosis requiring organ-specific therapy in the past 2 years
* Patients with cutaneous or ocular sarcoidosis, which in the opinion of the Investigator, are at risk for exacerbation, necessitating OCS rescue or other systemic therapy
* History of Addisonian symptoms that precluded previous OCS taper attempts
* Is an active, heavy smoker of tobacco/nicotine-containing products
* History of anti-synthetase syndrome or Jo-1 positive at Screening
* Patients with active tuberculosis or those currently undergoing treatment for tuberculosis

primary.m: Change from baseline in mean daily oral corticosteroid (OCS) dose at Week 48

abstracts:
Culver DA, Bonella F, Gupta R, Spagnolo P, Veltkamp M, Cameli P, et al. Efzofitimod versus placebo in patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis (EFZO-FIT): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial. Lancet Respir Med. 2026. doi: 10.1016/S2213-2600(26)00283-3
BACKGROUND: Oral corticosteroids are currently standard-of-care therapy for pulmonary sarcoidosis, but they are associated with substantial toxicity and reduced health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The EFZO-FIT trial aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of efzofitimod, a novel immunomodulatory fusion protein targeting the neuropilin 2 receptor, as a steroid-sparing agent in pulmonary sarcoidosis.
METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, adults aged 18-75 years with pulmonary sarcoidosis requiring treatment were enrolled at 85 study centres across nine countries (Brazil, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Spain, UK, and USA). Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 using stratified block randomisation to receive monthly intravenous infusions of efzofitimod 3 mg/kg, efzofitimod 5 mg/kg, or placebo over a 48-week treatment period, including a 12-week oral corticosteroid taper targeting 0 mg per day (starting on day 15). Oral corticosteroid dose could be adjusted upwards in the event of worsening sarcoidosis. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in mean daily oral corticosteroid dose at week 48. Outcome and safety analyses were done in participants who received at least one dose of the study drug and had at least one post-baseline efficacy assessment. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05415137) and is complete.
FINDINGS: Between Sept 22, 2022, and Aug 14, 2025, 331 patients were screened for inclusion. 63 were excluded and 268 participants were randomly assigned to receive placebo (n=91), efzofitimod 3 mg/kg (n=89), or efzofitimod 5 mg/kg (n=88). Four patients were excluded after random assignment (one in the placebo group and three in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group). 264 patients who received at least one dose of study treatment and had at least one post-baseline assessment were included in the outcome analysis and safety population (90 in the placebo group, 86 in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and 88 in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group). Among the 264 participants, the mean age was 53·8 years (SD 10·6); 114 (43%) of 264 patients were female and 150 (57%) were male. 168 (64%) identified as White. Mean steroid dose was 10·7 mg per day (SD 4·4) at baseline and 2·9 mg per day (4·5) at week 48. No difference was seen in the magnitude of oral corticosteroid taper between the active and placebo dose groups; the placebo-adjusted change from baseline was 0·02 mg per day in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (95% CI -1·49 to 1·52, p=0·98) and -0·73 mg per day in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group (-2·21 to 0·75, p=0·33). The percentage of participants with serious treatment-emergent adverse events was similar between groups. Malaise was more common in the placebo group (five [6%] of 90 patients vs zero in both efzofitimod groups). TEAEs that were more common in the efzofitimod groups included headache (17 [19%] of 88 patients in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group, 11 [13%] of 86 patients in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and four [4%] of 90 patients in the placebo group), sinusitis (nine [10%], six [7%], and two [2%] patients, respectively), wheezing (seven [8%], two [2%], and zero patients, respectively), and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) increased (five [6%], one [1%], and zero patients, respectively). Most adverse events were grade 1 or 2. Two participants died, both in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (one respiratory failure and one incarceration of a pre-existing inguinal hernia). Neither event was considered to be causally related to the treatment.
INTERPRETATION: Efzofitimod was well tolerated but did not result in lower steroid doses at week 48 compared with placebo. The results from steroid tapering indicate that oral corticosteroid doses can be more aggressively reduced in many patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis.
FUNDING: aTyr and Kyorin.

x.titre: Efzofitimod intraveineux contre placebo dans la sarcoïdose pulmonaire symptomatique sous corticoïdes
x.question: L'efzofitimod permet-il de réduire la dose quotidienne de corticoïdes oraux à 48 semaines chez des patients atteints de sarcoïdose pulmonaire ?
x.contexte:
La sarcoïdose est une granulomatose systémique de cause inconnue, dont l'atteinte pulmonaire est la plus fréquente. Elle peut entraîner dyspnée, toux, altération de la qualité de vie et fibrose pulmonaire dans les formes évoluées. Les corticoïdes oraux restent le traitement de première ligne, mais la plupart des patients nécessitent des traitements prolongés avec leurs effets indésirables cumulés. Le méthotrexate est le principal épargneur de corticoïdes, et aucun traitement n'a d'AMM spécifique dans cette indication en Europe.

L'efzofitimod est une protéine de fusion issue de l'histidyl-ARNt synthétase, qui se lie à la neuropiline-2 exprimée sur les cellules immunitaires (macrophages) et module l'inflammation granulomateuse. Il est administré par voie intraveineuse. Cette étude de phase 3 randomisée en double aveugle contre placebo compare deux doses (3 et 5 mg/kg) au placebo pendant 48 semaines, chez des adultes sous corticoïdes oraux stables, avec ou sans un immunosuppresseur. Le promoteur est aTyr Pharma, avec des centres français.
x.interet: L'étude porte sur l'épargne cortisonique dans la sarcoïdose pulmonaire, un objectif cliniquement pertinent en l'absence d'alternative approuvée. Elle pourrait faire émerger une nouvelle classe thérapeutique dans cette maladie.
x.profil: Des adultes atteints de sarcoïdose pulmonaire symptomatique, traités par corticoïdes oraux de façon stable.
inclusion: Sarcoïdose pulmonaire documentée depuis au moins 6 mois, avec preuve histologique et atteinte parenchymateuse sur l'imagerie
Sarcoïdose pulmonaire symptomatique : dyspnée mMRC ≥ 1 et score KSQ-Lung ≤ 70
Corticoïdes oraux depuis ≥ 3 mois, dose initiale de 7,5 à 25 mg/j stable depuis ≥ 4 semaines
exclusion: Biothérapie immunomodulatrice (anti-TNF, inhibiteur d'interleukine) ou antifibrosant
Fibrose pulmonaire probable (> 20 % au scanner haute résolution dans les 12 mois, ou CVF < 50 % avec KSQ-Lung < 30)
Atteinte cardiaque, neurologique ou rénale active nécessitant un traitement spécifique dans les 2 ans
Sarcoïdose cutanée ou oculaire à risque de poussée nécessitant un traitement systémique
Fumeur actif important, syndrome des antisynthétases ou anti-Jo-1 positifs, tuberculose active

bras.traitement: Efzofitimod 3 mg/kg par voie intraveineuse ; rythme non précisé
Efzofitimod 5 mg/kg par voie intraveineuse ; rythme non précisé

x.critere: Variation de la dose quotidienne moyenne de corticoïdes oraux entre l'inclusion et la semaine 48.
x.resultats: Dans l'essai de phase 3 publié (Lancet Respir Med 2026), 268 patients ont été randomisés : placebo (n=91), efzofitimod 3 mg/kg (n=89) ou 5 mg/kg (n=88). L'analyse a porté sur 264 patients (90, 86 et 88). La dose moyenne de corticoïdes oraux passait de 10,7 mg/j (ET 4,4) à l'inclusion à 2,9 mg/j (ET 4,5) à la semaine 48. Le critère principal n'est pas atteint : la différence ajustée vs placebo de la variation de dose était de 0,02 mg/j avec 3 mg/kg (IC 95 % -1,49 à 1,52 ; p=0,98) et de -0,73 mg/j avec 5 mg/kg (-2,21 à 0,75 ; p=0,33). Les événements indésirables graves étaient comparables entre les groupes. Céphalées (19 % à 5 mg/kg, 13 % à 3 mg/kg, 4 % sous placebo), sinusites (10 %, 7 %, 2 %), sifflements (8 %, 2 %, 0 %) et élévation des ASAT (6 %, 1 %, 0 %) étaient plus fréquents sous efzofitimod ; la plupart des événements étaient de grade 1 ou 2. Deux décès sont survenus dans le groupe 3 mg/kg (insuffisance respiratoire, incarcération d'une hernie inguinale), jugés non liés au traitement. Les auteurs concluent que l'efzofitimod est bien toléré mais ne réduit pas la dose de corticoïdes à 48 semaines, et que la décroissance protocolaire montre que les corticoïdes peuvent être diminués plus vite chez beaucoup de patients.
